औकारवर्ण: Aukāravarṇa — from the fourteenth face of the fourteen-faced Sāvarṇi Manu. Vā. 26. 46.
औगज: Augajas — a mantrakṛt and of Aṅgirasa branch. Vā. 59. 102.
औग्रसेनी: Augrasenī — the daughter of Ugrasena, and wife of Akrūra. Br. III. 71. 113.
औघवति: Aughavati — a R. sacred to Pitṛs. M. 22. 71.
औङ्क: Auṅka — a son of Bala. Vā. 88. 205.
औचेयु: Auceyu — a son of Bhadrāśva. M. 49. 5.
औत्कचेय: Autkaceya — a Rākṣasa clan after the name Utkaca. Br. III. 7. 140.
औत्कार्ष्टेय: Autkārṣṭeya — a Rākṣasa clan after Utkṛṣṭa. Br. III. 7. 140.
औत्तम: Auttama — see under Manu;1 devatas of;2 sons of;3 kṣa-triya-praṇetāraḥ. 1) M. 3. 47; Vā. 62. 3. 2) Vā. 62. 23-33. 3) Vā. 62. 34-35, 36.
औत्तानपाद: Auttānapāda — on the left cheek of Śiśumāra. Br. II. 23. 102.
औत्थानिककौतुक: Autthānikakautuka — a festivity connected with the child's first turning in bed; celebrated for Kṛṣṇa. Bhā. X. 7. 4, 5-6.
औदम्बरि: Audambari — a place of Ṛtudhāmāgni. Br. II. 12. 24; Vā. 29. 23.
औदक: Audakas — water fowls, of Tāmrā line. Vi. I. 21. 17.
औदार्य: Audārya — a son of Aṅgirasa. Vā. 65. 105.
औदुम्बर: Audumbaras — a class of seers. Bhā. III. 12. 43.
औद्गात्रम्: Audgātram — the Sāmans uttered by Udgātā in an yajña. Vi. III. 4. 12.
औद्भिदम्: Audbhidam — the hill on shore of the river Kṛtamālā. Br. III. 35. 17.
औपगवी: Aupagavī — name of Uddhava. Bhā. III. 4. 27.
औपधर्म्यम्: Aupadharmyam — propagated by the Lord for mislead-ing Asuras and other evil doers. Bhā. II. 7. 37.
औपमन्यु: Aupamanyu — a ṛtvik at the yajña of Brahmā. Vā. 106. 39.
Aupamanyus — a Vāsiṣṭha clan of sages. Br. III. 8. 98; M. 200. 11.
औरस: Aurasas — a tribe near the Gāndhāra region. M. 121. 46.
और्व: Aurva (I) — a son born of Apravāṇa (Apruvat-Matsya P.) and Ṛcī, being born from her thigh. Father of Ṛcīka. Jamadagni was his grandson; a mantrakṛt and sage.1 Sagara who had no son visited his hermitage with his two wives and was blessed for sons. Present at Sagara's Aśvamedha and other sacrifices and taught him the path to salvation;2 spoke to Sagara on the mode of worshipping Viṣṇu;3 on Varṇa-dharma;4 on Āśramadharma;5 on rituals;6 on the duties of the householder;7 on funeral rites;8 on the Śrāddha;9 pre-vented the pregnant queen of Bāhu(ka) from committing satī,10 and the posthumous son Sagara brought up in his hermitage to whom he did all samskaras. Was visited and revisited by Paraśurāma.11 Phalgutanta took refuge near his hermitage;12 extinguished the Tālajaṅgha line.13 Came to see Parīkṣit practising prāyopaveśa.14 A description of his hermitage.15 A sage of the Svārociṣa epoch, and one of the five Pravaras of Bhārgava gotra.16 1) Br. Aurva (II) — (Samvartaka, Vaḍavāmukha: s.v.). Hari took this form of fire and drank the waters of the sea;1 Brahmā fixed him in the Vaḍavāmukha ocean; celebrated for Aurvīmāyā (s.v).2 1) Br. II. 18. 80; III. 72. 17; M. 2. 5; Vā. 47. 76. 2) M. 121. 77; 175. 18, 58-72.
और्वशेय: Aurvaśeya — a son of Purūravas, became king; father of Nahuṣa; he was a dhārmic king and the sages performed a great sacrifice; the assembly looked like that of Indra when the Gandharvas sang, the Apsaras danced, the sages entered into debates and delivered sermons of all kinds. Vā. 2. 23-36.
और्वीमाया: Aurvī-Māyā — used by Maya to dispel the darkness of Tāmasāstra; earned by Hiraṇyakaśipu from Aurva in the Tārakāmaya war. M. 175. 20-71.
औशनसम्: Auśanasam — a tīrtham sacred to Pitṛs. M. 22. 31.
औशिज: Auśijas — a sage by garbha. Vā. 59. 90, 93.
औशीरपर्वत: Auśīraparvata — the hill noted for śrāddha and yajña performance; here grow all trees which could be used for yajñas. Br. III. 13. 29; Vā. 77. 29-31.
औष्टकर्ण: Auṣṭakarṇa — a kingdom watered by Hlādinī. Br. II. 18. 54.
